newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chronology of North Korean submarine drama.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of North Korean submarine drama.

text.p: The following is a chronology of events surrounding the North Korean submarine incursion.

Sept 18 - North Korean Shark-class submarine spotted by taxi driver stranded off beach near Kangnung on South Korea's east coast shortly after midnight. Massive manhunt is launched, using helicopters and sniffer dogs and, later, up to 60,000 troops. Weapons and clothes found on beach. Bodies of 11 infiltrators found shot dead, apparently in mass suicide. One North Korean captured alive. Authorities initially believe 20 North Koreans landed, later put number at 26.

Sept 19 - U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher urges "all parties" to avoid further provocative action. His comments infuriate Seoul, which expects U.S. condemnation. South Korean President Kim Young-sam slams "military provocation".
Sept 20 - Japan says incursion "deplorable".
Sept 21 - South Korean paratrooper killed by intruders in shootout, the first Southern casualty.
Sept 22 - Submarine captain and another agent killed.

Sept 23 - North Korea says submarine drifted South by accident due to engine failure, demands return of vessel and crew. Seoul dismissed explanation as "nonsense". U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry further enrages Seoul by calling on "both parties" to limit the damage.
Sept 24 - U.S. Defence Department condemns intrusion as "serious provocation" and violation of truce that ended 1950-53 Korean War.
Sept 26 - North Korean warns of "strong counter-measures".
Sept 27 - Pyongyang threatens "hundredfold or thousandfold" retaliation.
Sept 28 - Troops kill submarine's second-in-command. Two Koreas trade angry words in United Nations.
Sept 30 - Troops kill another infiltrator. Southern soldier killed by friendly fire.
Oct 1 - Kim Young-sam says South to review all aid to North Korea. South Korean diplomat found murdered in Vladivostok, Seoul media point finger at Pyongyang.
Oct 3 - Pyongyang denies involvement in diplomat's death.
Oct 5 - North Korea threatens "merciless retaliation", says "blood shall be paid with blood".
Oct 6 - Pyongyang says it has arrested a U.S. citizen, Carl Hunziker, as a spy.
Oct 9 - Troops find bodies of three South Korean civilians, one an elderly woman, apparently murdered by intruders.
Oct 12 - Washington's top official for Asia, Winston Lord, in Seoul to patch up ties with South Korea, insists "there have been no rifts in our alliance".
Oct 15 - U.N. Security Council demands Korean armistice be "fully observed". Pyongyang hints may scrap 1994 nuclear accord with Washington that froze its nuclear weapons programme.
Oct 16 - U.S. sends reconnaissance plane to monitor possible North Korean test firing of medium-range ballistic off coast of Japan. The firing never takes place.
Oct 17 - South Korean defence minister Lee Yang-ho removed, military top brass reshuffled, to "tigthen military discipline" following embarrassing submarine incursion.
Oct 21 - Kim Young-sam demands "clear apology" from North.
Oct 29 - Captured North Korean says submarine on spy mission and had no trouble evading Southern defences.
Nov 5 - Two more intruders shot and killed.
Nov 15 - North Korea says it can no longer keep its nuclear programme frozen.
Nov 19 - Pyongyang says it will abandon a border liaison office with the South.
Nov 23 -- Warren Christopher calls for "gesture" from Pyongyang to South.
Nov 24 - Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto says he supports Seoul demand for apology.
Nov 27 - Carl Hunziker freed by North Korea after intervention by U.S. congressmen Bill Richardson.
Nov 29 - Bill Richardson predicts Pyongang will apologise.
Dec 9 - U.S. diplomats urge North Korean envoys to issue apology during first in series of meetings in New York.
Dec 28 - Seoul foreign ministry says it has details of Pyongyang apology.
